profile.summary: Software developer at heart and open source contributor.

positions.title: Founding Engineer
positions.description:
Founding Engineer = day 0
Core engineer, multi-tasker and ball dropper.
Everything from initial design and jump-starting the software development process to co-creating the core data mover in the Kasten product.

positions.title: Contributor and Project Management Committee Member
Senior Consultant Software Engineer and Technical Team Lead
positions.description: Technical lead of the Maginatics file system metadata server team. On-boarded new developers to maintain robustness and code quality in the product. Continuously mentor team members in order to facilitate their technical and career growth. Continued individual contributions.

positions.title: Software Developer and Technical Team Lead
positions.description: Software Engineer specialized in scalability, reliability, concurrency and performance. Early member of the Maginatics engineering team. Made significant contributions to the design and implementation of the Maginatics cloud storage system, which provides a consistent file system interface for distributed object stores, such as AWS S3 and OpenStack Swift. Implemented a large number of features and optimizations in the file system metadata server, including among others, distributed locking and file map compression. Designed and carried out performance experiments and analysis, and implemented corresponding optimizations in the server. Diagnosed and fixed complex software defects.

positions.title: Systems Scientist Faculty
positions.description: Technical lead in the Data-Intensive Scalable Computing (DISC) and Cloud research projects in the Parallel Data Laboratory.  Designed, built, deployed and managed a cluster for data-intensive computing using Linux and the Apache stack for large-scale data processing (Hadoop/HDFS/HBase/Accumulo). Liaison for the CMU/Yahoo! collaboration on data-intensive computing.

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Performed research to overcome I/O bottlenecks encountered when storing the output produced by large parallel computer numerical  simulations. I wrote the parallel I/O implementation used in Carnegie Mellon's earthquake simulator (http://quake.ce.cmu.edu).
I developed techniques to compress, index and query large wavefield datasets in their compressed representation, that is, in the compressed domain. This approach turned an I/O intensive problem into a massively parallel computational workload, which is well suited for parallel many-core architectures.

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description: Built a software research prototype for pico-networks to share and bundle the internet connection of multiple devices.

positions.title: Visiting Researcher at the Center for Educational Computing Initiatives
Adjunct Instructor and Researcher
positions.description: Prepared and delivered lectures for the Computer Networks course for various terms.  Researcher in the Computer Networking Laboratory.

honors.title: SuperComputing Analytics Challenge
honors.description: Our work titled “Remote Runtime Steering of Integrated Terascale Simulation and Visualization”  won the Supercomputing Analytics Challenge.

honors.title: 2003 Gordon Bell Award for Special Achievement.
honors.description:
1st place along with the members of the Quake project. The milestone calculations for the award included:

The generation of a record unstructured hex mesh (3.7 billion elements, 4 billion nodes)
The largest unstructured mesh wave propagation simulation (900 million elements, 3.2 billion DOF)
The largest acoustic wave propagation inverse problem (17 million inversion parameters, 70 billion total unknowns)
The largest elastic wave propagation inverse problem (275,000 inversion parameters, around a billion total unknowns).
honors.issuer: Issued by ACM Supercomputing conference · Nov 2003

patents.title: Backing-Up Application Data From Cloud-Native Applications
patents.description: Embodiments described herein are directed to backing up and recovering cloud-native applications. In some embodiments, the data engine maps a first set of data volumes to a data repository dedicated to store a backup of the data associated with the application. Furthermore, the data engine transmits, using a dynamically generated process, the data stored in the identified first set of data volumes to the data repository for backup based on the mapping. The data engine may also initiate a recovery of the application. The data engine may use a new dynamically generated process to identify and transmit a respective data set to a corresponding data volume for storage. Moreover, the data engine may use the new process to restore the components of the application using each respective identified data set.

patents.title: Change Block Tracking In Cloud Orchestration Systems
patents.description: System, method, and computer program products for storing a snapshot of block-level changes in a data volume using a file system-level backup tool. An embodiment operates by receiving the block level changes in the snapshot from the data volume stored in an application in a cluster. The embodiment creates a root directory for the snapshot. The root directory may have one or more subdirectories. The embodiment maps one or more block changes in the data volume onto the one or more subdirectories and creates a manifest for identifying the snapshot in the file system-level backup tool. The manifest may be associated with the root directory. The embodiment then instructs the file system-level backup tool to store the snapshot by storing the root directory in content-addressable object storage based on the one or more subdirectories and storing the manifest in a manifest storage.
